title: Fidel Castro in JFK Records, 1959–2008
metaDescription: Fidel Castro led Cuba from 1959 until 2008 and is a principal subject of CIA operations in the JFK collection, including MONGOOSE and AMLASH.
h1: Fidel Castro in CIA operations in the JFK collection
lede: Fidel Castro led Cuba from the 1959 revolution until 2008 and was a principal subject of CIA operations discussed throughout the JFK Assassination Records Collection, including the MONGOOSE and AMLASH programs. BlackVaultDocs’ figure hub matches the name Fidel Castro in document titles from public NARA releases. The hub is a title index, not a history of Cuban governance and not a file count. PDFs remain on the originating archive.

sections.h2: What the Castro figure hub lists
paragraphs: The figure slug fidel-castro groups indexed titles that name Fidel Castro. The packet supplies no document count, so this page does not invent one. The public-record identity in the blurb is: led Cuba from the 1959 revolution until 2008; principal subject of CIA operations discussed throughout the JFK Assassination Records Collection, including the MONGOOSE and AMLASH programs.

MONGOOSE and AMLASH are the two program names in the packet. The blurb says the CIA operations discussed throughout the collection include those programs. It does not say how many titles name MONGOOSE, how many name AMLASH, or how many name Castro without either program. This overlay does not invent those splits.

1959 and 2008 are the bounds of Castro’s leadership of Cuba in the blurb. Those years are not a document date range for the JFK collection. This page keeps the leadership window and the collection name on separate lines. A title match is a catalog hit, not a finding that every page of the scan is an operational cable.

sections.h2: MONGOOSE, AMLASH, and the JFK Assassination Records Collection
paragraphs: The blurb places CIA operations, including MONGOOSE and AMLASH, as discussed throughout the JFK Assassination Records Collection. “Throughout” is qualitative. This page does not convert it into a percentage of the collection. Naming MONGOOSE and AMLASH is a citation of the packet, not an argument about what those programs achieved.

The related topic href on this packet is the JFK assassination collection, which matches the collection named in the blurb as an internal link. Researchers who need the scans should open the originating archive from the figure hub. BlackVaultDocs matches names in titles from public NARA releases; it does not re-host the PDFs.

sections.h2: How name matching works for Castro
paragraphs: Figure hubs match names in document titles from public NARA releases indexed on BlackVaultDocs. The Castro hub is that match, not a complete Cuba file and not a complete FOIA log. A missing title hit means the indexed title in this ingest did not match the name as implemented.

The all-figures directory lists other people in the same name index. Use the Castro hub for titles that name him. Use the collection link for the broader JFK posting. Program names in a title may appear without the personal name; those rows would not be promised by this name index.

sections.h2: What this page does not claim
paragraphs: This overlay does not argue that Castro ordered or did not order the assassination of President Kennedy. It restates the packet: led Cuba from the 1959 revolution until 2008; principal subject of CIA operations discussed throughout the JFK Assassination Records Collection, including MONGOOSE and AMLASH. Conspiracy commentary is outside the index.
No NARA ID is in the facts. No document total is in the facts. Cite 1959, 2008, MONGOOSE, AMLASH, and the JFK Assassination Records Collection. Do not attach an invented file count to Castro’s name.

The Fidel Castro figure hub is the live title list. All figures shows the rest of the name index. The JFK assassination collection is the related topic link on this packet. Open the originating archive for scans. A later ingest can retag titles; this prose still will not invent a document count.

MONGOOSE and AMLASH are program names in the packet. CIA operations discussed throughout the JFK Assassination Records Collection include those programs. Inclusion is not a title count for either cryptonym. A program title that omits Castro’s name would not be promised by this name index.

sections.h2: How to cite Fidel Castro on this site
paragraphs: Cite Fidel Castro as having led Cuba from the 1959 revolution until 2008 and as a principal subject of CIA operations discussed throughout the JFK Assassination Records Collection, including the MONGOOSE and AMLASH programs, as matched by name in indexed titles on BlackVaultDocs. Do not cite a document count from this guide. Do not treat the figure hub as a finding on the assassination. The source note is that figure hubs match names in document titles from public NARA releases indexed on BlackVaultDocs.

Cite 1959 and 2008 as the leadership window for Cuba. Cite MONGOOSE and AMLASH as named. Cite the JFK Assassination Records Collection as the home of those discussed operations. Do not attach a file count to Castro’s name from this guide.

faqs.q: How does Fidel Castro appear in the JFK declassified files?
faqs.a: The packet states that Fidel Castro led Cuba from the 1959 revolution until 2008 and was a principal subject of CIA operations discussed throughout the JFK Assassination Records Collection, including the MONGOOSE and AMLASH programs. BlackVaultDocs matches the name in indexed titles. This page does not assign a file count.

faqs.q: What years did Fidel Castro lead Cuba in this blurb?
faqs.a: The blurb states that he led Cuba from the 1959 revolution until 2008. Those years are the leadership window this page cites. They are not a document count and not a date range for every file in the JFK Assassination Records Collection. Titles that name Castro appear on the figure hub; PDFs remain on the originating archive.

faqs.q: What are MONGOOSE and AMLASH in the Castro files?
faqs.a: The blurb names MONGOOSE and AMLASH as programs included among CIA operations discussed throughout the JFK Assassination Records Collection. It does not count titles for each program. This page does not invent those counts. Open the figure hub and the originating archive for the scans.

faqs.q: Does the Castro figure hub prove a conspiracy in the Kennedy assassination?
faqs.a: No. The hub matches the name Fidel Castro in document titles from public NARA releases indexed on BlackVaultDocs. It restates the 1959–2008 leadership window and the CIA operations, including MONGOOSE and AMLASH, named in the blurb. It does not interpret those files as proof of a plot.

takeaways: Fidel Castro led Cuba from the 1959 revolution until 2008.
He was a principal subject of CIA operations discussed throughout the JFK Assassination Records Collection.
Those operations include the MONGOOSE and AMLASH programs as named in the blurb.
The figure hub matches that name in indexed titles; this packet supplies no document count.
This page does not treat title hits as a finding on conspiracy.
